question:
A 33-year-old woman with a history of multiple sclerosis in remission presents with 3 days of low back
pain following a prolonged car ride. She reports making frequent stops but did not adequately stretch
during these breaks. She denies leg pain, chest pain, shortness of breath, eye pain, or vision changes.
Physical examination reveals mild lumbar paraspinal tenderness, with 5/5 strength and intact sensation
in all extremities. Osteopathic examination identifies an L5 dysfunction that is extended, rotated, and
sidebent to the right. The sacral base is anterior on the right, and the inferior lateral angle (ILA) is
superior on the right. The straight leg test and Babinski test are both negative. What is the most likely
diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Bilateral sacral extension (B) Right rotation on a right oblique axis (C)
Left rotation on a right oblique axis (D) Right unilateral sacral extension (E) Bilateral sacral flexion (F)
Right rotation on a left oblique axis (G) Left unilateral sacral extension (H) Left rotation on a left oblique
axis (I) Right unilateral sacral flexion (J) Left rotation on a transverse axis
 A. Right rotation on a right oblique axis
B. Right rotation on a left oblique axis
C. Left rotation on a transverse axis
D. Right unilateral sacral flexion
E. Bilateral sacral extension
F. Left unilateral sacral extension
G. Right unilateral sacral extension
H. Left rotation on a right oblique axis
I. Left rotation on a left oblique axis
J. Bilateral sacral flexion
